arrived_at_port: This is when the vessel carrying your container arrives at the port. Your clearing agent can then continue the clearance work.
manifest_available: The manifest is the shipping line's list of everything on the vessel. Once it is available, customs can assess your PAAR.
paar_assessed: Customs assesses your PAAR (Pre-Arrival Assessment Report) and works out the duty to pay for your shipment. After this, the shipping line and the terminal can start their processing, and the duty can be paid.
duty_paid: This is when the import duty is paid. After it, customs can start its own processing.
en_route_to_bonded_terminal: Some containers are first moved to a bonded terminal, a secure area approved for goods still being cleared. This step applies only to some shipments.
shipping_line_processed: The shipping line finishes its own processing, including issuing the Delivery Order (DO) that allows your container to be released.
terminal_processed: The terminal finishes its own processing for your container.
customs_examination: Customs may physically examine a container to check the goods against the documents. This step applies only to some shipments.
customs_processed: Customs finishes its processing and releases your cargo. This can only happen after the duty is paid, and it must be done before the container can leave the port.
gate_out: This is when the gate pass and the EIR (Equipment Interchange Receipt) have both been issued and the container is out of the terminal.
in_transit: The container is on the road from the port to your delivery address.
delivered: The container has reached your delivery address. After unloading, the empty container must be returned to the terminal.
empty_container_returned: The empty container has been returned to the terminal. This completes the shipment.
